summary: Concurrent MaterialDNA repairCount lanes overlap the same source/test scope but encode different canonical ceilings. HG-BACKFILL-MATERIALDNA-COUNTERS (priority 5150, PR #313) explicitly requires rejection only above the exact IEEE-754 safe-integer boundary and tests 2^53-1 accepted / 2^53 rejected. HG-MATERIALDNA-REPAIRCOUNT-BOUND (priority 5080, PR #309) instead chooses a signed-31-bit ceiling of 2147483647 by analogy to recipeVersion. Because repairCount is a canonical count rather than the recipe revision identity counter, these patches are not merge-compatible and must not both integrate. The active independent HG-BACKFILL-MATERIALDNA-COUNTERS auditor should reconcile the semantic choice and the control plane should supersede/close the losing duplicate lane before merge.
evidence: .swarm/lanes/HG-BACKFILL-MATERIALDNA-COUNTERS.json: priority 5150; acceptance explicitly says repairCount rejects integers above the exact IEEE-754 safe-integer boundary.
.swarm/lanes/HG-MATERIALDNA-REPAIRCOUNT-BOUND.json: priority 5080; objective requires a bounded deterministic integer domain but does not specify 31-bit in acceptance.
PR #313 implements [0, 9007199254740991] with max/max+1 regressions; PR #309 implements a 2147483647 ceiling in the same MaterialDNA validation surface.
src/shared/Materials/MaterialDNA.luau on main currently bounds recipeVersion to 2147483647 but repairCount uses a separate non-negative-integer validator with no maximum.
